exactContract.type: Public sealed class deriving from System.Net.EndPoint. No IEquatable<NamedPipeEndPoint>, endpoint equality operator, or custom comparer is declared in this class.
exactContract.fields: Two constructor-assigned get-only string properties: ServerName and PipeName. The one-argument constructor supplies LocalComputerServerName "."; the two-argument constructor retains the supplied strings without normalization.
exactContract.equality: Equals(object?) requires a NamedPipeEndPoint and compares ServerName and PipeName in their original roles with string ==. These are case-sensitive ordinal string comparisons, not pipe-name normalization or an OS-level name equivalence rule.
exactContract.hash: GetHashCode() returns ServerName.GetHashCode() ^ PipeName.GetHashCode(), with no custom comparer or cache.
exactContract.logicalReview: Under the ordinary string equality/hash contract, equal endpoint tuples produce equal component hashes and therefore equal XOR hashes. Unequal endpoints sharing a hash do not violate that contract. No numeric hash stability, distribution, runtime cost, or end-to-end performance claim was tested.
exactContract.restrictedAlgebra: For the reviewed built-in local-server producer, ServerName is the same "." string. XOR by its fixed hash is a bijection on the pipe-name hash value: h1 XOR c equals h2 XOR c exactly when h1 equals h2. This observation is restricted to that producer shape, is not a benchmark, and does not establish universal immateriality.
exactContract.normalInputBoundary: Properties and constructors are annotated non-nullable. Null injection, OS pipe-name edge validation, and changing equality/validation/default conventions are not proposed or exercised.
exactContract.comparerDocumentation: Pinned dotnet/docs best-practices-strings.md lines210 and321 explicitly describe default string equality-operator ordinal semantics. Guessed external hash-remarks paths returned404 and remain failures, not retrieved authority.
